description: An engineering initiative focused on autonomous software and lightweight system architecture. The goal for this challenge is to build an offline-first onboard tool that tracks crew vitals in real time and catches health anomalies early without relying on Earth connectivity. All about practical engineering, low resource usage, and shipping a clean, working prototype
summary:
AEGIS-BIO is a proof-of-concept autonomous closed-loop life-support kernel and 3D anatomical digital twin designed for deep-space EVA suits during cis-lunar and Mars missions. With up to 22-minute radio delays, astronauts cannot rely on Houston if a suit malfunctions or the crew loses consciousness. Current spacesuit Caution & Warning Systems (CWS) only trigger passive alarms after critical thresholds are breached.
Our MVP demonstrates a new paradigm: building a self-reliant survival system from scratch using deterministic mathematical physics (Runge-Kutta ODE integration, Adaptive Kalman filtering, Mahalanobis covariance detection, and Model Predictive Control) that operates completely independently of heavy, hallucination-prone LLMs. It detects physiological drift 90 seconds earlier than threshold alarms and autonomously actuates oxygen purge, LBNP counter-pressure, and radiation shielding in under 2 milliseconds—laying the foundation for a future two-tier architecture with a specialized micro-AI for unprecedented emergencies
details:
1. MY CORE VISION & ARCHITECTURAL PHILOSOPHY

In deep space, a 22-minute One-Way Light Time (OWLT) radio delay means that an astronaut experiencing acute hypoxia, decompression, or Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS) is completely on their own. Current spacesuit Caution & Warning Systems (CWS) on the ISS EMU and Artemis xEMU are passive and reactive: they wait until inspired ppCO2 or SpO2 crosses a hard threshold and sound an alarm requiring human action. Conversely, many modern software proposals attempt to plug general-purpose local LLMs directly into life-support control—an approach I consider fundamentally unsafe for flight avionics due to high power consumption, non-deterministic latency, and the risk of fatal hallucinations

What I built for this hackathon is a functional proof-of-concept and minimal engineering prototype of a two-tier survival architecture:

- Tier 1 (Implemented in this Prototype — The Deterministic Zero-AI Spinal Cord): I strongly believe that an autonomous life-support system must first be engineered from the ground up using pure mathematical physics and control theory, capable of operating with zero dependency on existing local AI models. Even if higher-level compute fails, this deterministic core filters sensor noise, isolates mechanical faults from human pathology, and physically keeps an unconscious astronaut alive in under 2 milliseconds

- Tier 2 (Future Roadmap — Custom Specialized Micro-Model for "Unknown Unknowns"): Once the deterministic survival loop is mathematically guaranteed via Lyapunov stability, the next stage of development is to build or fine-tune a dedicated, ultra-compact specialized neural model (such as a Physics-Informed Neural Network or State-Space Mamba/Liquid micro-architecture) strictly as an advisory supervisory layer. In deep space, astronauts will inevitably encounter complex, cascading "black swan" emergencies that no human engineer or pre-programmed rulebook ever anticipated. This specialized model will sit above the mathematical kernel—predicting non-obvious cross-organ failure cascades and synthesizing novel parameter setpoints for unprecedented situations, while the underlying MPC and Lyapunov kernel enforces hard physiological safety envelopes

2. PRINCIPLE OF OPERATION: 12-FUNCTION MATHEMATICAL KERNEL

I engineered the backend (`closed_loop_kernel.py`) around 12 deterministic mathematical and biophysical functions interacting with a real-time 3D WebGL anatomical twin:

1. 4th-Order Runge-Kutta (RK4) Coupled ODE Integrator (`rk4_ode_step`): Numerically integrates nonlinear differential equations governing suit gas concentration and intracranial compliance

2. Alveolar Gas & Bohr-Haldane Dissociation Model (`alveolar_bohr_haldane_model`): Couples alveolar PAO2 with a carbon-dioxide-shifted Hill oxyhemoglobin curve where hypercapnic acidosis shifts P50 rightwards

3. Monro-Kellie Exponential Intracranial Compliance (`monro_kellie_icp_dynamics`): Models SANS intracranial pressure (ICP) and Optic Nerve Sheath Diameter (ONSD) via exponential elastance P = P0 * exp(E * dV) under microgravity fluid shifts and LBNP counter-suction

4. Two-Compartment Bone Calcium & Renal Kinetics(`two_compartment_calcium_renal_kinetics`): Tracks osteoclastic trabecular demineralization and urinary calcium oxalate supersaturation

5. Linear-Quadratic Hematopoietic Radiation Kinetics (`hematopoietic_radiation_repair_ode`): Computes bone marrow stem-cell DNA repair and survival fraction under Artemis AstroRad HDPE selective shielding

6. Adaptive 1D Kalman Filter with Chi-Square NIS Gate (`run_kalman_sensor_filter`): Physical struggle inside a pressurized suit causes severe chest ECG motion spikes (+88 bpm). My filter computes Normalized Innovation Squared (NIS); when NIS > 11.5, it dynamically scales measurement noise covariance R_k to reject false electrode spikes without blinding the monitor

7. Cholesky-Decomposed Multivariate Mahalanobis Detector (`cholesky_mahalanobis_anomaly_detector`): Computes D_M(x) = ||L^-1 (x - mu)||_2 via lower-triangular Cholesky factorization across a 5D state vector [ICP, HR, SpO2, ppCO2, RadFlux] to catch subtle coupled drift 90 seconds before single-channel alarms

8. Welch Spectral Autonomic Index (`welch_spectral_autonomic_index`): Computes the LF/HF sympathetic stress ratio from RR-intervals using a Hann-windowed Fast Fourier Transform (FFT)

9. Bayesian Fault-Tree Isolator (`bayesian_fault_tree_isolator`): Evaluates posterior probabilities P(H_i | E) to distinguish suit hardware failures (scrubber saturation, pressure leak) from crew pathology

10. Model Predictive Control (MPC) Projected Gradient Solver (`mpc_projected_gradient_solver`): Continuously optimizes the control vector u* = [O2_purge_Lpm, LBNP_mmHg] over a future prediction horizon under a strict 480W spacecraft emergency battery constraint

11. Control Lyapunov Stability Verifier (`lyapunov_stability_margin`): Evaluates V(x) = 0.5 * e^T P e and verifies dV/dt <= 0 at every tick to mathematically prove asymptotic convergence back to homeostasis

12. LZ77 Entropy Compressor & MIL-STD-1553B CRC-16 Encoder (`lz77_dsn_telemetry_compressor`): Packs actuator command words with CRC-16 checksums and compresses 64Hz telemetry buffers by >96% into compact Deep Space Network (DSN) clinical burst packets

3. WHAT I DEMONSTRATED & VERIFIED IN THIS PROTOTYPE

- 3 Historical & Extreme Survival Scenarios: Interactive 3D X-ray showcase reconstructing (1) the 2013 ISS EVA-23 fan/separator failure with CO2 flooding and ECG electrode noise, (2) the August 1972 Apollo Class-X Solar Proton Storm with SANS ICP elevation, and (3) a rapid decompression blackout where the astronaut loses consciousness (0% motor response) and the Dead-Man's Switch autonomously executes a full closed-loop rescue

- Procedural Multi-Fault Synthesizer & Live Autonomous Sandbox: Judges can spawn random, unlabeled compound failures in real time and observe a live A/B benchmark comparing a simulated Legacy NASA Threshold CWS against my continuous gradient solver—proving a >65% reduction in cumulative homeostasis deviation.

- 500-Trial Blind Monte Carlo Verification Suite (`/api/validate`): Built-in statistical test harness executing 500 randomized crisis trials in ~15ms, proving >80% Kalman RMSE error reduction, +90s early detection lead time on empirical capnography traces, and >98% closed-loop survival

4. TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES & HARDWARE TARGETS

- Backend & Mathematical Engine: Python 3.13, FastAPI, NumPy (linear algebra, Cholesky decomposition, FFT, RK4 ODEs), Zlib (LZ77 compression & CRC-16).

- Frontend & 3D Visualization: TypeScript, Next.js 16, React, Three.js / React Three Fiber (custom anatomical X-ray shaders, procedural WebAudio synthesizer), Tailwind CSS, deployed with an autonomous client-side WASM/JS fallback solver on Vercel

- Target Avionics Profile: Engineered for <150 KB RAM and <2ms execution to support future porting to `no_std` Rust on radiation-hardened flight processors (BAE RAD750 / NASA HPSC)

Amd finnaly winning a prize is not my primary goal. What matters most to me is drawing attention to the underlying architectural concept - pushing aerospace and life-support engineering to think deeper about true closed-loop autonomy and real-time adaptive systems when human lives are on the line. Trusting machines with human survival is never easy, especially millions of kilometers from Earth. Yet if we build the deterministic mathematical foundation properly first, and carefully layer specialized adaptive intelligence on top, autonomous systems can respond to unforeseen crises faster and more reliably than any remote command center - potentially saving countless missions and lives :)
